sourceNote: Domains that host third-party social/messaging platforms, shared by two independent call sites: transactional-flow.ts never follows a link to one of these (a social platform is never a booking engine), and crawl.ts never treats a page whose crawl redirects out to one of these as part of the audited site. Migrated one-for-one from the previous hardcoded SOCIAL_PLATFORM_HOSTS array; every pattern below matched something a real crawl actually hit before being added, per social-hosts.ts's original doc comment.

patterns.rationale: Confirmed on a real haaitza.com crawl: a stub link (e.g. /facebook) redirecting into facebook.com is slow and often errors out under headless conditions, and was previously misreported as a broken internal link.
Same social-icon-link pattern as Facebook; SMB sites commonly link an Instagram profile from the header/footer.
Legacy Twitter domain, still widely linked from existing site footers alongside x.com.
Common B2B footer link, never a page of the audited site.
Channel/profile links, and embedded-video click-through targets.
Locale-specific TLDs (pinterest.fr, pinterest.co.uk, etc) all resolve to the same profile-page platform.
WhatsApp click-to-chat short link, never a page of the audited site.
WhatsApp's own domain, same reasoning as wa.me.
